topics.topic: Refusal reason and retry treatment for import confirmation after migration closure
questions: Do the generic keep-and-retry rules exclude a confirmation refused because another accepted import has already created the closure?
When the same session resubmits the confirmation that already accepted the import, is it refused at stage (1) because its one-time confirmation value is gone, or because the migration closure exists?

quotes: An accepted import drops the uploaded file of every owner session (M11); a confirmation shown in another session is refused because the import is closed (rule 8).
When the closure exists, uploading, showing the mapping or the import's confirmation step and confirming are refused, and a sign-out goes on.
Stage (1) comes first — the session, the CSRF value and the confirmation value, used up when it was carried (A13 rule 6) — and this refusal comes before every other of the import's own checks.
judgement.why: An accepted import drops every session's upload and the closure prevents every further import step, while a same-session resubmission is first refused because its one-time confirmation value was consumed.

topics.topic: Ownership and production of the unauthenticated sign-in form
questions: Who admits and produces the initial sign-in form, and the sign-in form shown after an invalid or expired session, when the surface decides nothing and `sign_in_owner` is the credential submission rather than the form read?

quotes: `module:owner_interface` renders the sign-in form and every page, sets and reads the session cookie and carries the CSRF value in every form; it decides nothing (A13 rules 1, 5, 7).

The sign-in form posts the credential;
   `capability:operations.perform_owner_operation` hands it to
   `capability:owner_sessions.sign_in_owner`, which is the one owner request
   made without a session and checks only the lockout and the credential
   (A13 rule 4).

`module:owner_interface` shows the sign-in form
  for a request without a valid session.
judgement.why: The owner interface produces the form for an initial or invalid-session request, and its submission is handed through operations to the named sign-in capability without requiring an owner session.
